In [[mathematics]], a '''Fricke involution''' is the [[involution (mathematics)|involution]] of the [[modular curve]] ''X''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') given by τ&nbsp;→&nbsp;–1/''N''τ. It is named after [[Robert Fricke]]. The Fricke involution also acts on other objects associated with the modular curve, such as spaces of [[modular form]]s and the [[Jacobian variety|Jacobian]] ''J''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') of the modular curve.  The quotient of ''X''<sub>0</sub>(''N'') by the Fricke involution is a curve called ''X''<sub>0</sub><sup>+</sup>(''N''), and for ''N'' prime this has genus zero only for a finite list of primes, called [[Supersingular_prime_(moonshine_theory)|supersingular primes]], which are the primes that divide the order of the [[Monster group]].
